title: Audit ingest connector for customer-managed sinks and VPC bindings
creator: Samir Patel
description: Build a robust 'audit ingest connector' that enables Private/VPC/on-prem deployments to reliably forward audit events to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS/Blob) using multiple transport modes (signed-resumable uploads, proxy-shared, mTLS push). This ticket focuses on the connector interface, provenance envelope format, resumable transfer semantics, CMEK/KMS handshake patterns, and operator controls for retention and throttling. The goal is to provide a single pluggable component that integrates with the existing audit pipeline while addressing air-gapped and high-compliance environments.
acceptance_criteria: Connector can be configured in three modes: direct signed-resumable upload (customer bucket), egress-proxy (customer-managed gateway), and push-over-mTLS to on-prem collector.
Uploads support resumable chunking with idempotent receipts and byte-range verification to survive restarts.
Provenance envelope schema v1 documented: transport metadata, sequence id, source node, SHA256 envelope, and optional audit policy tags.
CMEK handshake documented: key-wrapping flow for server-side encryption, replay protection, and KMS rotation compatibility.
RBAC v2 controls enforced at connector level: only admin roles can change sink bindings and retention, plus audit events for config changes emitted to internal audit stream.
Failure modes test coverage: network intermittent, 429 throttling, auth expiry, object-lease conflicts — connector retries with exponential backoff and circuit-breaker behavior.
Operator console shows connector health, backlog size, last successful offset, and per-sink rate estimates; alerts wired to SRE runbook.
Security review completed and threat model updated to include new credential flows and encryption key exposures.
E2E demo that forwards 10k synthetic events to a customer bucket with SSE-KMS enabled and validates integrity and ordering.
Migration guide for existing audit-forwarder users describing mapping to new connector config and rollback steps.
notes: We intentionally avoid creating a new 'shipper' binary; connector will be a pluggable module that can run inside audit-forwarder or as a sidecar for on-prem deployments.
Design must support both short-lived signed URLs (for cloud buckets) and pre-established storage bindings (for long-running on-prem flows).
Consider using a small provenance envelope to keep customer storage schemas unchanged while enabling integrity checks and replay protection for our internal reconciler.
RBAC v2 implications: changes to sink bindings must generate an immutable audit event to internal infra-audit stream and be subject to SSO admin approvals in Console.
comments: 2026-03-01 Samir Patel: Kickoff meeting held with Security and SRE. Agreed on three-mode transport and provenance envelope baseline. Action: Lina to draft schema and handshake flows.
2026-03-04 Lina Gomez: Initial schema v0.1 uploaded to Confluence (link below). Chose chunked-resumable with 64MB default chunk size; open question on per-chunk signing vs single envelope signature.
2026-03-06 Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed handshake — requested addition of nonce + timestamp to prevent replay when using signed URLs. Also requested mandatory TLS1.3 for proxy mode.

2026-03-09 Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Ran failure injection locally — connector recovered from token expiry when refresh flow correctly implemented. Observed higher memory during backlog; plan to add local on-disk queue cap and eviction policy.
2026-03-11 Design review: UX team gave thumbs-up on operator surface. Action: PM to own migration guide and schedule customer communications for beta.
